# SEO-056: Self-canonicalize each paginated page rather than the series entry point

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

## Statement

Page two and beyond of a paginated sequence declare their own address as canonical, not the address of the first page in the sequence.

## Rationale

Canonicalizing a sequence onto its first page tells the engine the later pages are duplicates of it, so the items that appear only on those pages are dropped from consideration along with the URLs that hold them.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "pagination"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Include the page parameter or path segment in the canonical value for every page after the first. If the intent is instead to expose the whole set at one address, build a view-all page and canonicalize the sequence to that, not to page one.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Fetch at least the second and third page of a paginated sequence and confirm each declared canonical carries its own page identifier.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: none.

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: none recorded.
